task: Write an internal historical Council record of no more than 160 words, based only on the supplied excerpts. Distinguish the two texts, outcomes and failure mechanisms. Record each proposed approach and the limit of any agreement. Attribute any supplied delegation detail to the right speaker and capacity. Use the supplied evidence IDs. Label any suggested next step as analysis.
scope: A new information structure for an already exposed event family. Two fictional file desks can possess overlapping sets of the same two exact historical source cards. This simulates evidence delivery, not historical speech, votes, preferences or private negotiations.

public.US-VOTE: On 28 February 2019 the United States submitted S/2019/186. It received nine votes in favour, three against and three abstentions. China and the Russian Federation voted against it as permanent members, and the draft was not adopted.
public.RU-VOTE: S/2019/190 was a separate Russian draft. It received four votes in favour, seven against and four abstentions and failed to reach the required number of affirmative votes.
public.US-TEXT: The U.S. draft called for a peaceful process toward credible presidential elections under international observation. It proposed unhindered humanitarian access and assistance across Venezuela consistent with humanitarian principles.
public.RU-TEXT: The Russian draft supported inclusive national dialogue, including the Montevideo Mechanism. It placed Venezuela’s Government in the lead on humanitarian assistance and called for its consent and appeal.

CHAIR.text: Ndong Mba of Equatorial Guinea announced both results as Council President. Equatorial Guinea itself abstained on S/2019/186 and voted for S/2019/190.

INDONESIA.text: Indonesia abstained on both drafts. Its representative, Dian Triansyah Djani, urged inclusive political dialogue and called on all parties to accept the Secretary-General's good offices.

criteria.D1: Names the U.S. draft, records 9–3–3 and attributes non-adoption to negative votes from China and Russia as permanent members.
criteria.D2: Names the Russian draft, records 4–7–4 and attributes non-adoption to too few affirmative votes.
criteria.A1: States the U.S. draft proposed a peaceful electoral process with international observation.
criteria.A2: States the Russian draft supported inclusive national dialogue, including the Montevideo Mechanism.
criteria.P1: Distinguishes Ndong Mba’s Council presidency from Equatorial Guinea’s abstention on the U.S. draft and affirmative vote on the Russian draft.
criteria.P2: Records Indonesia’s two abstentions and attributes its inclusive dialogue and Secretary-General good-offices appeal to Indonesia.
criteria.C1: Records that both drafts addressed humanitarian assistance.
criteria.C2: Distinguishes the texts’ humanitarian approaches: unhindered access in the U.S. text and a government-led, consent-based approach in the Russian text.
criteria.S1: Does not treat either failed draft as creating Council authority.
criteria.S2: Supplies a clearly labeled analytical next step without attributing a new commitment to the Council or a delegation.

critical_errors: Claims either draft was adopted or assigned new Council authority.
Conflates the veto of the U.S. draft with the shortage of affirmative votes on the Russian draft.
Treats the procedural announcement as Equatorial Guinea’s national endorsement.
Misattributes either national position or invents a material commitment.
